(Without Paired DNA) Integrated Pipeline for Identifying Tumor Subclones

Jiazhen Rong, Chi-Yun Wu, Zhang Lab, University of Pennsylvania

2024-08-27

Introduction

This tutorial aims to provide an integrated pipeline example for when paired DNA data is not available.

In this tutorial, we will use a spatial transcriptomics colorecral carcinoma dataset generated by our study (10x Genomics chemistry, will be available upon publication).

Load Data

library(Clonalscope)
library(Seurat)
library(AUCell)
library(Matrix)
library(dplyr)
library(Seurat)
library(patchwork)

# load example data from standard 10x genomics format} 
mtx <- readMM("data/V11Y04-378-A1/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/matrix.mtx.gz") 
barcodes <- read.table("data/V11Y04-378-A1/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/barcodes.tsv.gz", stringsAsFactors = F, sep='\t', header=F) 
features <- read.table("data/V11Y04-378-A1/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/features.tsv.gz", stringsAsFactors = F, sep='\t', header=F) 
colnames(mtx) <- barcodes[,1]
rownames(mtx) <- features[,1]
# load spatial spot_datainates
spot_data = as.data.frame(read.table("data/V11Y04-378-A1/spatial/tissue_positions_list.csv",sep=","))
colnames(spot_data) <-c("barcode","include","row","col","image_row","image_col")
rownames(spot_data) <- spot_data[,1]
gene_symbols = features[,2] # Gene Symbol

# set file path for results results
dir_path = "your_output_path";dir.create(dir_path,recursive = T)

Initial Estimation of Normal Reference

In the recent update, we have add function FindNormalReference() for automatically get an initial estimation of normal cells, which will be utilized as control/reference cells for CNV estimation.

However, to get the most refined and accurate annotation, users with professional knowledge on the disease and tumor related biomarkers could view this specific tutorial for annotating tumor/normal cells when paired DNA is not available.

  • Option 1: Based on the marker genes

    We utilizes Seurat to clustering the cells/spots into transcriptionally different clusters and check for enrichment of common single cell gene signatures from MSigDB SCSig collection [1]. For this CRC example, we set tissue_type to be Large_Intestine and input several keywords of known normal celltypes. The keywords of known normal cell type shall be separated with “|”.

    For the full list of available tissue types, please type ?FindNormalReference().

    # Identify
normal_celltype=c("immune|endothelial|stromal|fibroblast|Goblet_Progenitor|Secretory_Progenitor")
initial_normal_spots = FindNormalReference(counts=mtx, gene_symbols=gene_symbols,method="marker",marker_source="MSigDB",tissue_type="Large_Intestine",normal_celltype = normal_celltype)

  • Option 2: Based on the First Principal Component

    Alternatively, previous study [3] suggests a quick identification of normal spots via (1) taking the first principal component of PCA of the data and (2) performs Kmeans clustering with K=2 on the first component of PCA. The clusters with lower gene expression is assigned as normal spots.

    To utilize PCA based separation instead of marker genes, the following commands could be run:

    initial_normal_spots = FindNormalReference(counts=mtx, gene_symbols=gene_symbols,method="pca")

Then prepare the initial normal reference into Clonalscope input format:

# setting normal/reference cells in the annotation file
celltype = barcodes; rownames(celltype) = barcodes[,1]
celltype$annotation = "tumor"
celltype[initial_normal_spots,"annotation"] = "normal"

Clustering on All Cells/Spots

Now we can run the subclone detection on all cell/spot barcodes.

Here we show the pipeline with the initial estimated normal cells as reference and with chromosomal arm level segments for initial estimation.

# Size of each chromosome (hg19 and GRCh38 are provided.)
size=read.table("../Clonalscope/data-raw/sizes.cellranger-GRCh38-1.0.0.txt", stringsAsFactors = F)
# List of cyclegenes retrieved from the "CopyKAT"package (https://github.com/navinlabcode/copykat)
cyclegenes=readRDS("../Clonalscope/data-raw/cyclegenes.rds")
# bed file indicating gene positions (hg19 and GRCh38 are provided.)
bed=read.table("../Clonalscope/data-raw/hg38.genes.bed", sep='\t', header = T)

# Generate segmentation table for each chromosome arm (w/o paired WGS)
chrarm=read.table("../Clonalscope/data-raw/cytoarm_table_hg38.txt", stringsAsFactors = F, sep='\t', header=T)
chrarm=chrarm[order(as.numeric(chrarm[,1]),as.numeric(chrarm[,3])),]
bin_bed=chrarm[,-2]

seg_table_filtered=data.frame("chr"=bin_bed[,1], 'start'=as.numeric(bin_bed[,2]),
                              'end'=as.numeric(bin_bed[,3]), 'states'=1, 'length'=as.numeric(bin_bed[,3])-as.numeric(bin_bed[,2]),
                              'mean'=0, 'var'=0, 'Var1'=1:nrow(bin_bed),'Freq'=50000,
                              'chrr'=paste0(bin_bed[,1],":", bin_bed[,2]), stringsAsFactors = F)

# Filtering HLA and cell cycle genes
Input_filtered <- FilterFeatures(mtx=mtx, barcodes=barcodes, features=features, cyclegenes=cyclegenes)

# Remove raw inputs
rm(mtx); rm(barcodes); rm(features)

# normally run Clonalscope algorithm
Cov_obj <- RunCovCluster(mtx=Input_filtered$mtx, barcodes=Input_filtered$barcodes,
                         features=Input_filtered$features, bed=bed,alpha=5,beta=5,
                         celltype0=celltype, var_pt=0.99, var_pt_ctrl=0.99, include='all',
                         alpha_source='all', ctrl_region=NULL,
                         seg_table_filtered=seg_table_filtered, size=size,
                         dir_path=dir_path, breaks=50, prep_mode = 'intersect', est_cap = 2,
                         clust_mode='all')
saveRDS(Cov_obj,paste0(dir_path,"Cov_obj_chrarm.rds"))

Final Tumor/Normal Assignment based on CNV Loads

Finally, the tumor and normal status could be assigned based on CNV loads based on MalignantAssignment() function.

Cov_obj <- readRDS(paste0(dir_path,"Cov_obj_chrarm.rds"))
final_tn_res <- MalignantAssignment(Cov_obj,cutoff=0.5)

We can visualize the clustering result that’s only on tumor spots in space:

clusters_clonalscope = cbind(barcode=names(Cov_obj$result_final$result$Zest), # barcode
                             clusters=Cov_obj$result_final$result$Zest)        # clusters

clusters_clonalscope = clusters_clonalscope[names(final_tn_res$final_assignment)[final_tn_res$final_assignment == "Tumor"],] # only keep tumor spots based on final assignment
  
SpatialPlot(spot_data,clusters_clonalscope,save=T,dir_path,title="Clonalscope Clustering on Tumor Spots",cluster=T,pt_size=4)
